name: correctness-cache-race-stale-ttl
description: Go PR adding an in-process TTL cache to a user repo. The new cache.go has zero mutex protection around its map (Go panics on concurrent map read/write), and repo.go violates the file-level locking invariant — documented in the package comment at lines 1–7 of repo.go — by writing the cache from Get under an RLock. The package comment is only visible with full-file context; reviewers seeing only the hunk won't know about the contract.

expected.description: Cache.Lookup and Cache.Put both read/write `c.entries` (a Go map) with no synchronisation. The package-level comment claims read-path can be lock-free 'because Repo.Set is the only writer' — but Put is also called from Repo.Get on cache miss, so multiple goroutines concurrently mutate the map. Triggers `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write` under load.

Repo.Get calls `r.cache.Put(id, u)` while holding only `r.mu.RLock()`. The file's package comment (lines 4–7) explicitly states 'every read AND every write must acquire mu' as a write — this hunk silently violates that invariant, allowing multiple reader goroutines to mutate the cache map concurrently.

Cache has no eviction or compaction — entries beyond their TTL stay in the map forever, so memory grows unbounded over time. Lookup correctly rejects expired entries but Put never reclaims their slot.
